root_idea.summary: The root centers on completion: reaching the intended end, full measure, or perfection.
root_idea.development: The lexical pattern extends from being or becoming complete or perfect to bringing something to completion in Form IV; كَامِلٌ denotes what has reached its full measure or intended completeness.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Presented under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَكْمَلَ rather than the inflected QAC lemma candidate.
Presented under the normalized masculine singular active-participle citation form كَامِلٌ; the Quranic occurrence is feminine.
Inflected dual active-participle form of كَامِلٌ, represented under the same normalized dictionary headword.

senses.definition: To complete, bring to full measure, or perfect something.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive Form IV; in the Quran it is used for completing a prescribed measure or course and for bringing a religious order to perfection.

senses.definition: Complete or full, having reached the whole measure or intended fulfillment of something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally, including with a duration, number, quantity, or burden, to indicate that the relevant whole or full measure has been attained; its gender and number vary with the noun modified.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become perfect; in some usage, to become complete, entire, whole, or full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I verb describing the attainment or emergence of completeness or perfection.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fully developed in bodily vigor, having reached the customary term of physical maturity; consummate or perfect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical specialization of كَامِلٌ concerning developed bodily strength or maturity.
Plural noun for optional religious acts performed beyond the obligatory service.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The unit's completion, perfection, wholeness, and fullness branches are represented across the Form I classical meaning and the Quran-attested completion senses.
The bodily-vigor and maturity specialization is represented separately as Classical Arabic.
Pointer-only cross-reference with no independent lexical definition.
The specialized noun for supererogatory religious acts is represented as a Classical meaning.

cautions: The feminine and dual Quranic forms grouped under كَامِلٌ are presented together under the normalized masculine singular active-participle citation form.
